title: Adic gradient estimates and finite-level differentiation of series
statement:
Let $F$ be a field of arbitrary characteristic, $n\geq0$, $D=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $\mathfrak n=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset D$, $P=F[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\subset D$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $J=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset P$. Write $\partial_i$ for the termwise partial derivatives on $D$ [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. For every integer $s\geq1$ and every $f\in\mathfrak n^s$, one has $\partial_i f\in\mathfrak n^{s-1}$ for all $i$. In particular, for every polynomial $g\in J^r$, $r\geq1$, its polynomial gradient $(\partial g/\partial t_i)_i$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] embedded in $D^n$ belongs to $(\mathfrak n^{r-1})^{\oplus n}$, and its polynomial and series partial derivatives agree. For every $h\in D$ and $r\geq1$, let $p_{r+1}(h)\in P$ consist of the terms of $h$ of total degree $<r+1$. Then
$$h-p_{r+1}(h)\in\mathfrak n^{r+1},\qquad \partial_i h-\partial_i p_{r+1}(h)\in\mathfrak n^r.$$
For $Q_r=D/\mathfrak n^r$, with universal derivation $\mathrm d:Q_r\to\Omega_{Q_r/F}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], one has the finite-level identity
$$\mathrm d(h\bmod\mathfrak n^r)=\sum_{i=1}^n(\partial_i h\bmod\mathfrak n^r)\,\mathrm d(t_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r).$$
No division by integers or characteristic-zero assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal), the one-power Leibniz bound; Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), polynomial differentiation. Agent-written total-degree coefficient and polynomial approximation argument, extracted from returned parent proof steps 3 and 7; the tags do not state the formal-series finite-level identity themselves.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with coefficient ring $F$ and base ideal $0$: for $k\ge1$, membership in $\mathfrak n^k$ is equivalent to vanishing of all coefficients of total degree $<k$, since $0^{k-|E|}=0$ for $|E|<k$. If $s\ge2$ and $|E|<s-1$, then $|E+e_i|=|E|+1<s$. By the coefficient formula in [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative], $[t^E]\partial_i f=(E_i+1)[t^{E+e_i}]f=0$. The criterion gives $\partial_i f\in\mathfrak n^{s-1}$. For $s=1$ the conclusion is simply membership in $D=\mathfrak n^0$.

source.place: Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal), Leibniz bound; Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), polynomial differential formula; explicit coefficient/truncation argument.

proof.text: For a polynomial $g=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha t^\alpha$, the polynomial monomial formula [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] gives coefficient $(E_i+1)c_{E+e_i}$ at $t^E$ in $\partial_i g$, exactly the series formula [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. Thus the two partial derivatives agree coefficientwise. The inclusion $P\to D$ sends every generator of $J$ into $\mathfrak n$, so it sends every finite sum of products defining $J^r$ into $\mathfrak n^r$. Applying Step 1 with $s=r$ to $g$ gives every asserted gradient coordinate bound.

source.place: Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal), Leibniz bound; Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), polynomial differential formula; explicit coefficient/truncation argument.

proof.text: There are finitely many multi-indices of total degree $<r+1$ (each coordinate is at most $r$), so $p=p_{r+1}(h)$ is a polynomial [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Its coefficients agree with those of $h$ below that degree. The coefficient criterion [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with base ideal zero therefore puts $h-p$ in $\mathfrak n^{r+1}$. Additivity of the formal partial derivatives [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative], Step 1 with $s=r+1$, and Step 2 give $\partial_i h-\partial_i p\in\mathfrak n^r$.

source.place: Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal), Leibniz bound; Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), polynomial differential formula; explicit coefficient/truncation argument.

proof.text: Let $q:D\to Q_r$ be the quotient map. The map $p\mapsto\mathrm d(q(p))$ is an $F$-derivation from $P$ to the $P$-module $\Omega_{Q_r/F}$. By the universal property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] it factors through a $P$-linear map $\Omega_{P/F}\to\Omega_{Q_r/F}$ sending $\mathrm d t_i$ to $\mathrm d(q(t_i))$. Apply this map to the polynomial identity of [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] for $p=p_{r+1}(h)$. Step 3 gives $q(h)=q(p)$ and $q(\partial_i h)=q(\partial_i p)$, yielding exactly the stated finite-level identity. If $n=0$, $D=P=F$, the variable ideals vanish, the truncation is $h$, and $\Omega_{F/F}=0$ by its defining relations, so the same identity is the empty sum. All integer factors above are multiplications in $F$, never divisions.

lean.statement: theorem adic_gradient_control (F : Type u) [Field F] (n : ℕ) : (∀ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s → ∀ f : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F, f ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F))) ^ s → ∀ i : Fin n, pderiv F i f ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F))) ^ (s - 1)) ∧ (∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → ∀ g : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F, g ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (MvPolynomial.X : Fin n → MvPolynomial (Fin n) F))) ^ r → ∀ i : Fin n, ((MvPolynomial.pderiv i g : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F))) ^ (r - 1)) ∧ (MvPolynomial.pderiv i g : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) = pderiv F i (g : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F)) ∧ (∀ (h : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) (r : ℕ), 1 ≤ r → (h - (truncTotal (r + 1) h : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F))) ^ (r + 1)) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, pderiv F i h - pderiv F i (truncTotal (r + 1) h : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F))) ^ r) ∧ KaehlerDifferential.D F (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F ⧸ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F))) ^ r) (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ h) = ∑ i : Fin n, Ideal.Quotient.mk ((Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F))) ^ r) (pderiv F i h) • KaehlerDifferential.D F (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F ⧸ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F))) ^ r) (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (X i)))
